A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Transformer SAT-solving work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Sections 5.3 and 6 and Appendix B report original compiled-solver accuracy, reasoning-length and attention-sensitivity experiments, plus trained-model generalization results.

after.justification: Sections 5.1 and 6 and Appendix B retain original experiments and additionally report full-trace correctness and further generalization results.

M1.justification: The seven-layer, five-head SAT construction, DPLL reasoning procedure, training objective, and appendix SAT-solver code remain unchanged. The revised greedy-decoding notation and expanded mathematical treatment do not establish a different implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic 3-SAT under marginal, random, and skewed distributions over 4–20 variables, with training ranges 6–10 and 11–15. v2 Figure 6 reports results for evaluation scenarios already described in v1 Section 6.2.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain models trained on all three distributions and the compiled solver. Newly discussed systems such as NeuroSAT, MatSAT, and SATformer are related work, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds full-trace correctness across within-length and length-generalization evaluations. Checking every generated token against abstract DPLL, while allowing different valid decision orders, substantially strengthens the evaluation criterion beyond final SAT/UNSAT accuracy. Training budgets and data settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a diagnostic comparison of answer correctness and reasoning-trace validity, exposing their different failure patterns as problem size changes. The existing CoT-length analysis and soft-attention sensitivity experiment are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Dataset accuracy averages and mean/maximum CoT-length reporting use the same practices.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds 18 full-trace correctness entries and changes the three marginal-test accuracies for 11–15 variables from 98.66/99.70/99.57% to 99.82/99.89/99.81%. Figures 3 and 6 add trace-validity curves and further distribution-specific results. The PDFs do not explain whether the changed accuracies reflect corrections or reruns.

T1.justification: v2 adds explicit encoding definitions, clause-operation lemmas and proofs, and saturated-attention approximation derivations. Appendix C.7 introduces transition-system refinement and revises the CoT-to-DPLL state mapping, replacing v1's bijective trace-equivalence definition. The main theorem's resource bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central SAT-construction, PARAT, and generalization contributions remain. However, v2 elevates softmax-induced length limitations into an introductory claim about fixed Transformer weights, whereas v1 Section 5.3 presented soft attention as a possible explanation.

C2.justification: v2 more directly interprets length-generalization failures as theoretical predictions and attributes exponential worst-case CoT requirements to NP-hardness. It also explains how failure to emit a terminal token within the context limit can produce below-chance accuracy.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies PARAT's restricted program syntax, output interface, and terminal-token scoring rules. It removes v1's exact compiled-model width of 502 and parameter count of 5,011,862. Appendix A's training hyperparameters and the SAT-solver source remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands to formal-reasoning benchmarks, symbolic-solver-assisted LLMs, and neural SAT solvers. v2 credits MatSAT when introducing its encoding and develops a more explicit distinction between PARAT's construction goals and Tracr's interpretability goals.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and construction explanation undergo substantial rewriting. Most PARAT feature and compilation material moves from the main text to Appendix D, while SAT preliminaries and the correctness argument are reorganized and expanded.

P2.justification: v2 adds the encoding illustration in Figure 2 and four-panel Figure 6, expands Table 1 into answer/trace blocks, and adds dashed trace curves and revised legends to the main generalization figure. Figure 1 gains input/output labels; the existing CoT-length and attention-sensitivity plots are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: Full-trace evaluation improves empirical scrutiny: Table 1 distinguishes, for example, 99.81% answer accuracy from 86.06% valid traces. However, the revised theoretical treatment introduces problems: Definition C.19 omits requiring successor states to remain related, leaving Proposition C.20 unsupported as written, and Appendix C.1 incorrectly removes a satisfied literal instead of its clause. These weaknesses in the central theoretical explanation offset clear empirical and presentation gains enough to prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
